verses.39:1: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah in the tenth year of King Zedekiah—this was the eighteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
verses.39:2: And the army of the king of Babylon laid siege against Jerusalem, and Jeremiah was kept under guard in the court of the prison, which is in the house of the king,
verses.39:3: where King Zedekiah had shut him up, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving this city into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it,
verses.39:4: and Zedekiah shall by no means escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, for he shall surely be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon, and his mouth shall speak to his mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes,
verses.39:5: and Zedekiah shall enter into Babylon, and there he shall dwell.'"
verses.39:6: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.39:7: "Behold, Hanamel, the son of Shallum your father's brother, is coming to you, saying, 'Buy for yourself my field which is in Anathoth, for the right is yours to take it for a possession.'"
verses.39:8: And Hanamel, the son of Samol my father's brother, came to me into the court of the prison and said, "Buy my field which is in the land of Benjamin, which is in Anathoth, for the right is yours to buy it, and you are the elder." And I knew that it was the word of the Lord.
verses.39:9: And I bought the field of Hanamel, the son of my father's brother, and weighed out to him seven shekels and ten of silver.
verses.39:10: And I wrote in a scroll and sealed it, and called witnesses to attest it, and weighed the silver on a balance.
verses.39:11: And I took the scroll of purchase, the one that was sealed,
verses.39:12: and I gave it to Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the sight of Hanamel, the son of my father's brother, and in the sight of the men who stood by and wrote in the scroll of purchase, and in the sight of the Jews who were in the court of the prison.
verses.39:13: And I charged Baruch in their sight, saying,
verses.39:14: "Thus says the Lord Almighty: 'Take this scroll of purchase and the scroll that was read, and you shall place it in an earthen vessel, that it may endure for many days.'
verses.39:15: For thus says the Lord: 'Fields and houses and vineyards shall yet be established in this land.'"
verses.39:16: And I prayed to the Lord after I had given the scroll of purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, saying,
verses.39:17: "O Lord, the One who is, You have made heaven and earth by Your great power and by Your high and uplifted arm; nothing shall by any means be hidden from You,
verses.39:18: showing mercy to thousands, and repaying the sins of fathers into the bosom of their children after them—the great, the mighty God,
verses.39:19: the Lord of great counsel and mighty in works, the great God, the Almighty, and the Lord of great name; Your eyes are upon the ways of the sons of men, to give to each one according to his way;
verses.39:20: You who performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt even to this day, both in Israel and among the earthborn, and made for Yourself a name, as it is this day,
verses.39:21: and brought forth Your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and with wonders, with a mighty hand,
verses.39:22: and with an uplifted arm, and with great visions; and You gave them this land, which You swore to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.39:23: And they entered in and possessed it, yet they did not listen to Your voice, nor walk in Your ordinances; all that You commanded them they did not do, so that all these evils came upon them.
verses.39:24: Behold, a multitude has come to the city to seize it; and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword and the famine; as You have spoken, so it has come to pass.
verses.39:25: Yet You say to me, 'Buy for yourself the field with silver'—and I wrote a scroll and sealed it, and called witnesses to attest it—though the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans!"
verses.39:26: Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.39:27: "I am the Lord, the God of all flesh; shall anything be hidden from Me?
verses.39:28: Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: This city shall surely be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it;
verses.39:29: and the Chaldeans who fight against this city shall come and burn this city with fire, and burn down the houses upon whose rooftops they offered incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke Me to anger.
verses.39:30: For the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have been doing only evil in My sight from their youth;
verses.39:31: for this city has been for My anger and for My wrath from the day they built it even to this day, that I should remove it from My presence,
verses.39:32: because of all the evils of the sons of Israel and of Judah which they have done to provoke Me to anger—they, and their kings, and their rulers, and their priests, and their prophets, the men of Judah and those who dwell in Jerusalem.
verses.39:33: And they turned their back to Me, and not their face; though I taught them early in the morning and taught them again, yet they did not listen any longer to receive instruction.
verses.39:34: And they set their defilements in the house upon which My name is called, in their impurities.
verses.39:35: And they built the altars to Baal which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to offer up their sons and their daughters to Molech the king—things which I did not command them, nor did it enter My heart—to do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.
verses.39:36: And now thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the city of which you say, 'It shall be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon by the sword, and by famine, and by banishment':
verses.39:37: Behold, I will gather them from all the earth where I have scattered them in My anger and in My wrath and in great indignation; and I will bring them back to this place, and I will cause them to dwell securely.
verses.39:38: And they shall be to Me a people, and I will be to them a God.
verses.39:39: And I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me all their days, and for good to them and to their children after them.
verses.39:40: And I will make with them an everlasting covenant, which I will by no means turn away from behind them; and I will put My fear into their heart, so that they shall not depart from Me.
verses.39:41: And I will visit them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, and with all My heart and with all My soul.
verses.39:42: For thus says the Lord: Just as I have brought upon this people all these great evils, so I will bring upon them all the good things that I have spoken concerning them.
verses.39:43: And fields shall yet be bought in the land of which you say, 'It shall be untrodden by man and beast, and they have been delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans';
verses.39:44: and they shall buy fields with silver, and you shall write a scroll and seal it, and call witnesses to attest it, in the land of Benjamin, and round about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the hill country of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negev; for I will turn back their captivities."
verses.40:1: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still bound in the court of the prison, saying,
verses.40:2: "Thus says the Lord, who makes the earth and forms it to establish it—the Lord is His name:
verses.40:3: Call to Me, and I will answer you, and I will declare to you great and mighty things, which you have not known.
verses.40:4: For thus says the Lord concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the king of Judah, which have been torn down for ramparts and bulwarks,
verses.40:5: to fight against the Chaldeans, and to fill it with the dead bodies of the men whom I struck down in My anger and in My wrath, and from whom I turned away My face because of all their evils:
verses.40:6: Behold, I will bring upon it healing and a cure, and I will reveal to them—and I will heal it—both peace and faithfulness;
verses.40:7: and I will turn back the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel, and I will build them as at the first.
verses.40:8: And I will cleanse them from all their iniquities by which they have sinned against Me, and I will by no means remember their sins by which they sinned against Me and departed from Me.
verses.40:9: And it shall be for gladness, and for praise, and for majesty to all the people of the earth, who shall hear of all the good things that I will do; and they shall fear and be embittered concerning all the good things and concerning all the peace that I will make for them.
verses.40:10: Thus says the Lord: There shall yet be heard in this place, of which you say, 'It is desolate, without man and beasts,' in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem that are laid waste because there is neither man nor beasts,
verses.40:11: the voice of gladness and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say, 'Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, for the Lord is good, for His mercy is forever'; and they shall bring gifts into the house of the Lord; for I will turn back all the captivity of that land as at the first," says the Lord.
verses.40:12: Thus says the Lord of hosts: "There shall be in this desolate place, because there is neither man nor beast, and in all its cities, resting places of shepherds who cause sheep to lie down.
verses.40:13: In the cities of the hill country, and in the cities of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negev, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the places round about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, sheep shall yet pass by the hand of one who counts them," says the Lord.
verses.41:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord—and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and all his army, and all the land of his dominion were fighting against him, against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah—saying:
verses.41:2: "Thus says the Lord: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah, and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord: This city shall surely be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he shall capture it and burn it with fire,
verses.41:3: and you shall by no means escape from his hand, and you shall surely be captured and given into his hands, and your eyes shall see his eyes, and you shall enter into Babylon.
verses.41:4: Yet hear the word of the Lord, O Zedekiah king of Judah! Thus says the Lord:
verses.41:5: In peace you shall die; and as they wept for your fathers who reigned before you, they shall weep for you also, and even to Hades they shall lament for you; for I have spoken a word, says the Lord.'"
verses.41:6: And Jeremiah spoke all these words to King Zedekiah in Jerusalem.
verses.41:7: And the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against the cities of Judah, and against Lachish and against Azekah, for these remained among the cities of Judah as fortified cities.
verses.41:8: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah had concluded a covenant with the people to proclaim release,
verses.41:9: that every man should send away his manservant and every man his maidservant, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, free, so that no man of Judah should serve as a slave.
verses.41:10: And all the nobles and all the people who had entered into the covenant to send away each one his manservant and his maidservant turned back, and they forced
verses.41:11: them to be manservants and maidservants.
verses.41:12: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
verses.41:13: "Thus says the Lord: I made a covenant with your fathers in the day that I delivered them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, saying,
verses.41:14: 'When six years are fulfilled, you shall send away your Hebrew brother who shall be sold to you and shall serve you six years, and you shall send him away free.' Yet they did not listen to Me, nor did they incline their ear.
verses.41:15: And they turned today to do what is right before My eyes, to proclaim release, every man for his neighbor, and they concluded a covenant before Me in the house upon which My name has been called.
verses.41:16: And you turned back and profaned My name in bringing back every man his manservant and every man his maidservant, whom you had sent away free according to their own will, to be manservants and maidservants to you.
verses.41:17: Therefore thus says the Lord: You have not listened to Me to proclaim release, every man to his neighbor. Behold, I proclaim a release for you—to the sword, and to death, and to famine—and I will give you over to dispersion among all the kingdoms of the earth.
verses.41:18: And I will give the men who have transgressed My covenant, who have not upheld My covenant which they made before Me, the calf which they made to serve it,
verses.41:19: the princes of Judah and the rulers and the priests and the people,
verses.41:20: and I will give them to their enemies, and their carcasses shall be food for the birds of the heaven and for the beasts of the earth.
verses.41:21: And Zedekiah king of Judea and their princes I will give into the hands of their enemies, and the army of the king of Babylon is for those who flee from them.
verses.41:22: Behold, I command," says the Lord, "and I will bring them back to this land, and they shall fight against it, and take it, and burn it up with fire, and the cities of Judah, and I will make them desolate, without inhabitants."
verses.42:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim king of Judah, saying:
verses.42:2: "Go to the house of Archabein, and you shall bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the courts, and you shall give them wine to drink."
verses.42:3: And I brought out Jeconiah the son of Jeremin, the son of Chabasein, and his brothers, and his sons, and all the house of Archabein,
verses.42:4: and I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of the sons of Jonan the son of Hananiah, the son of Gedaliah, a man of God, which is near the house of the princes who are above the house of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the court.
verses.42:5: And I set before them a jar of wine and cups, and I said, "Drink wine."
verses.42:6: And they said, "We will by no means drink wine, for Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, 'You shall by no means drink wine, you and your sons forever,
verses.42:7: and you shall not build a house, and you shall not sow seed, and you shall not have a vineyard, for you shall dwell in tents all your days, that you may live many days upon the land where you sojourn.'
verses.42:8: And we have obeyed the voice of Jonadab our father, so as not to drink wine all our days, we and our wives, and our sons and our daughters,
verses.42:9: and not to build houses to dwell there; we have had neither vineyard nor field nor seed;
verses.42:10: and we have dwelt in tents, and have obeyed and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.
verses.42:11: And it came to pass when Nebuchadnezzar came up against the land, that we spoke of entering, and we entered into Jerusalem from before the army of the Chaldeans and from before the army of the Assyrians, and we have been dwelling there."
verses.42:12: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
verses.42:13: "Thus says the Lord: Go and say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, 'Will you not receive instruction to listen to My words?
verses.42:14: The sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have upheld the word which he commanded his children, not to drink wine, and they have not drunk; yet I spoke to you early in the morning, and I spoke, and you did not listen.
verses.42:15: And I sent to you My servants the prophets, saying, "Turn back, every man from his evil way, and make your deeds better, and do not go after other gods to serve them, and you shall dwell upon the land which I gave to you and to your fathers." Yet you did not incline your ears, and you did not listen.'
verses.42:16: And the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have upheld the commandment of their father, but this people has not listened to Me.
verses.42:17: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing upon Judah and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evils that I have spoken against them.
verses.42:18: Therefore thus says the Lord: Because the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have obeyed the commandment of their father, to do just as their father commanded them,
verses.42:19: there shall never be lacking a man of the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab standing before Me all the days of the earth."
verses.43:1: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.43:2: "Take for yourself a scroll of a book, and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you against Jerusalem, and against Judah, and against all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah, even to this day.
verses.43:3: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the evils that I purpose to do to them, that they may turn back from their wicked way, and I will be merciful to their iniquities and to their sins."
verses.43:4: Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah, and he wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord, which He had spoken to him, upon a scroll of a book.
verses.43:5: And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, "I am kept under guard; I am not able to enter into the house of the Lord.
verses.43:6: And you shall read from this scroll in the hearing of the people in the house of the Lord on a day of fasting; and in the hearing of all Judah who come from their city you shall read to them.
verses.43:7: Perhaps their plea for mercy will fall before the face of the Lord, and they will turn back from their wicked way; for great are the wrath and the anger of the Lord that He has spoken against this people."
verses.43:8: And Baruch did according to all that Jeremiah commanded him, reading from the book the words of the Lord in the house of the Lord.
verses.43:9: Now it came to pass in the eighth year of King Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, that all the people in Jerusalem and the house of Judah proclaimed a fast before the Lord.
verses.43:10: Then Baruch read from the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the house of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the Lord, and in the hearing of all the people.
verses.43:11: And Micaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the Lord from the book.
verses.43:12: And he went down to the king's house, into the house of the scribe; and behold, all the princes were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah the son of Shelemiah, and Jonathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
verses.43:13: Then Micaiah declared to them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read in the hearing of the people.
verses.43:14: And all the princes sent to Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, saying, "The scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people, take it in your hand and come." So Baruch took the scroll and went down to them.
verses.43:15: And they said to him, "Read again in our hearing." So Baruch read.
verses.43:16: Now it came to pass, when they had heard all the words, that they took counsel, each one with his neighbor, and said, "We shall surely declare to the king all these words."
verses.43:17: And they questioned Baruch, saying, "Where did you write all these words?"
verses.43:18: And Baruch said, "From his own mouth Jeremiah declared to me all these words, and I wrote them in a book."
verses.43:19: Then they said to Baruch, "Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah; let no man know where you are."
verses.43:20: And they went in to the king in the court, and they gave the scroll to be kept in the house of Elisha, and they declared all the words to the king.
verses.43:21: Then the king sent Jehudi to bring the scroll; and he took it from the house of Elisha, and Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and in the hearing of all the princes who stood around the king.
verses.43:22: Now the king was sitting in the winter house, and a brazier of fire was before him.
verses.43:23: And it came to pass, when Jehudi had read three or four columns, that he cut them off with the scribe's razor and cast them into the fire that was on the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed in the fire that was on the brazier.
verses.43:24: And they did not inquire, nor did they tear their garments—the king and his servants who heard all these words.
verses.43:25: And Elnathan and Gedaliah advised the king to burn the scroll.
verses.43:26: And the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son and Seraiah the son of Azriel to seize Baruch and Jeremiah; but they hid themselves.
verses.43:27: Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll—all the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah—saying,
verses.43:28: "Again, take another scroll for yourself, and write all the words that were on the scroll which King Jehoiakim burned;
verses.43:29: and you shall say, 'Thus says the Lord: You have burned this scroll, saying, "Why have you written on it, saying, 'The king of Babylon shall surely come and destroy this land, and man and beast shall vanish from it'?"
verses.43:30: Therefore thus says the Lord against Jehoiakim king of Judah: He shall have no one sitting on the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out in the heat of the day and in the frost of the night.
verses.43:31: And I will punish him, and his offspring, and his servants; and I will bring upon him, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the land of Judah, all the evils that I have spoken against them, and they did not listen.'"
verses.43:32: So Baruch took another scroll and wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim had burned; and still more words like these were added to it.
verses.44:1: Now Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned in place of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king to reign over Judah.
verses.44:2: But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land listened to the words of the Lord, which He spoke by the hand of Jeremiah.
verses.44:3: And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah, saying, "Pray now for us to the Lord."
verses.44:4: Now Jeremiah came and went through the midst of the city, and they had not put him into the prison house.
verses.44:5: And the army of Pharaoh went out from Egypt; and the Chaldeans heard the report of them, and went up against Jerusalem.
verses.44:6: Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.44:7: "Thus says the Lord: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah, who sent to you to inquire of Me, 'Behold, the army of Pharaoh, which has come out to help you, shall return to the land of Egypt,
verses.44:8: and the Chaldeans themselves shall come back and fight against this city, and they shall capture it and burn it with fire.
verses.44:9: For thus says the Lord: Do not suppose in your souls, saying, "The Chaldeans will surely depart from us," for they shall by no means depart.
verses.44:10: And even if you strike down the whole army of the Chaldeans who fight against you, and there remain some who are pierced through, each one in his place, these shall rise up and burn this city with fire.'"
verses.44:11: And it came to pass, when the army of the Chaldeans went up from Jerusalem from before the army of Pharaoh,
verses.44:12: that Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin, to buy from there in the midst of the people.
verses.44:13: And he was at the Gate of Benjamin, and there was a man with whom he lodged, Saruia the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah, saying, "Are you fleeing to the Chaldeans?"
verses.44:14: And he said, "Falsehood! I am not fleeing to the Chaldeans." But he did not listen to him; and Saruia seized Jeremiah and brought him to the princes.
verses.44:15: And the princes were embittered against Jeremiah and struck him, and they sent him into the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made that into a prison house.
verses.44:16: So Jeremiah went into the house of the pit and into the Chereth, and he remained there many days.
verses.44:17: Then Zedekiah sent and called him, and the king asked him secretly to tell him, "Is there a word from the Lord?" And he said, "There is; into the hands of the king of Babylon you shall be delivered."
verses.44:18: Moreover Jeremiah said to the king, "What wrong have I done to you, and to your servants, and to this people, that you put me into a prison house?
verses.44:19: And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Babylon shall by no means come against this land'?
verses.44:20: And now, O lord the king, let my plea for mercy fall before your face; and why do you send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, that I may not die there?"
verses.44:21: Then the king gave command, and they cast him into the prison house, and they gave him one loaf of bread each day from outside where they bake, until the loaves failed from the city; and Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
verses.45:1: And Saphanias the son of Nathan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, and Jehucal the son of Shelemiah heard the words which Jeremiah was speaking to the people, saying,
verses.45:2: "Thus says the Lord: 'He who dwells in this city shall die by the sword and by famine, but he who goes out to the Chaldeans shall live; and his life shall be for a prize, and he shall live.'
verses.45:3: For thus says the Lord: 'This city shall surely be delivered into the hands of the army of the king of Babylon, and he shall capture it.'"
verses.45:4: And they said to the king, "Please, let that man be put to death, for he weakens the hands of the fighting men who remain in the city and the hands of all the people, by speaking to them according to these words; for this man does not prophesy peace to this people, but only evil."
verses.45:5: And the king said, "Behold, he is in your hands." For the king could not prevail against them.
verses.45:6: And they cast him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, which was in the court of the guard, and they lowered him into the cistern. And in the cistern there was no water, but only mire; and he was in the mire.
verses.45:7: And Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian, and he was in the house of the king, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern; and the king was at the Gate of Benjamin.
verses.45:8: And he went out to him, and spoke to the king, and said,
verses.45:9: "You have done wickedly in what you have done, to kill this man because of the famine; for there is no longer any bread in the city."
verses.45:10: And the king commanded Ebed-Melech, saying, "Take into your hands thirty men from here, and bring him up out of the cistern, lest he die."
verses.45:11: And Ebed-Melech took the men and went into the underground house of the king, and took from there old rags and old ropes, and threw them to Jeremiah into the cistern,
verses.45:12: and he said, "Put these underneath the ropes." And Jeremiah did so.
verses.45:13: And they drew him with the ropes and brought him up out of the cistern; and Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
verses.45:14: And the king sent and called him to himself into the house of Aseleisel, which was in the house of the Lord. And the king said to him, "I will ask you a matter, and please do not hide a word from me."
verses.45:15: And Jeremiah said to the king, "If I declare it to you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will by no means listen to me."
verses.45:16: And the king swore to him, saying, "As the Lord lives, who made this soul for us, I will surely not kill you, nor will I give you into the hands of these men."
verses.45:17: And Jeremiah said to him, "Thus says the Lord: 'If you indeed go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, your soul shall live, and this city shall by no means be burned with fire; and you and your house shall live.
verses.45:18: And if you do not go out, this city shall be delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and you shall by no means be saved.'"
verses.45:19: And the king said to Jeremiah, "I am anxious about the Jews who have fled to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hands, and they mock me."
verses.45:20: And Jeremiah said, "They shall by no means hand you over. Hear the word of the Lord which I speak to you, and it shall be better for you, and your soul shall live.
verses.45:21: And if you refuse to go out, this is the word which the Lord has shown me:
verses.45:22: And behold, all the women who were left in the house of the king of Judah were being led out to the princes of the king of Babylon, and they were saying, 'Your men of peace have deceived you and shall prevail against you; and they shall bring down your feet in slippery places; they have turned away from you.'
verses.45:23: And they shall bring out your wives and your children to the Chaldeans, and you shall by no means be saved, for you shall be captured by the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city shall be burned down."
verses.45:24: And the king said to him, "Let no man know of these words, and you shall by no means die.
verses.45:25: And if the princes hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Declare to us, what did the king speak to you? Do not hide it from us, and we will by no means put you to death. And what did the king speak to you?'
verses.45:26: then you shall say to them, 'I am casting my plea for mercy before the eyes of the king, that he would not send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
verses.45:27: And all the princes came to Jeremiah and questioned him; and he declared to them according to all these words which the king had commanded him. And they kept silent, because the word of the Lord was not heard.
verses.45:28: And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard until the time when Jerusalem was captured.
verses.46:1: And it came to pass in the ninth month of Zedekiah king of Judah, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem, and they besieged it;
verses.46:2: and in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was breached;
verses.46:3: and all the leaders of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the Middle Gate: Marganasar, and Samagoth, and Nabusachar, and Nabusareis, Nagargasnaser, Rabamath, and the rest of the commanders of the king of Babylon.
verses.46:14: And they sent and took Jeremiah from the court of the guard, and delivered him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan; and they brought him out, and he dwelt in the midst of the people.
verses.46:15: And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in the court of the guard, saying,
verses.46:16: "Go and speak to Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian, 'Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing My words upon this city for evil and not for good,
verses.46:17: and I will save you in that day, and I will by no means give you into the hands of the men before whose face you are afraid.
verses.46:18: For I will surely save you, and you shall by no means fall by the sword; and your life shall be for a prize, because you have trusted in Me, says the Lord.'"
verses.47:1: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard from Daman had sent him away, when he had taken him in shackles in the midst of the captivity of Judah who were being led to Babylon.
verses.47:2: And the captain of the guard took him and said to him, "The Lord your God has spoken these evils against this place,
verses.47:3: and the Lord has done it, because you have sinned against Him and have not heeded His voice.
verses.47:4: Behold, I have loosed you from the shackles that were on your hands. If it is good in your sight to come with me to Babylon, then I will set my eyes upon you;
verses.47:5: but if not, depart; return to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed in the land of Judah, and dwell with him in the midst of the people in the land of Judah; to wherever is good in your eyes to go, go." And the captain of the guard gave him gifts and sent him away.
verses.47:6: And he came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and dwelt in the midst of the people who were left in the land.
verses.47:7: And all the commanders of the army that was in the field, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah in the land, and they entrusted to him men and their wives whom he had not carried away to Babylon.
verses.47:8: And there came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Jophe the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of the Maachathite, they and their men.
verses.47:9: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, saying, "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be better for you.
verses.47:10: And behold, I dwell before you at Mizpah, to stand before the Chaldeans who may come to you. But as for you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them into your vessels, and dwell in the cities that you have occupied."
verses.47:11: And all the Jews who were in Moab, and among the sons of Ammon, and those in Idumea, and those in all the land, heard that the king of Babylon had given a remnant to Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.
verses.47:12: And they came to Gedaliah in the land of Judah, to Mizpah, and gathered wine, and summer fruit in very great abundance, and oil.
verses.47:13: And Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the army who were in the fields came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,
verses.47:14: and they said to him, "Do you indeed know that Baalis king of the sons of Ammon has sent Ishmael to you to strike down your life?" But Gedaliah did not believe them.
verses.47:15: And Johanan said to Gedaliah secretly in Mizpah, "Let me go now and strike down Ishmael, and let no one know, lest he strike down your life, and all Judah who are gathered to you be scattered, and the remnant of Judah perish."
verses.47:16: And Gedaliah said to Johanan, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely concerning Ishmael."
verses.48:1: Now it came to pass in the seventh month that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elasa, of the lineage of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah at Mizpah; and they ate bread together there.
verses.48:2: Then Ishmael arose, and the ten men who were with him, and struck down Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land,
verses.48:3: and all the Jews who were with him in Mizpah, and all the Chaldeans who were found there.
verses.48:4: And it came to pass on the second day after he had struck down Gedaliah, when no one knew it,
verses.48:5: that men came from Shechem, from Salem, and from Samaria—eighty men, with their beards shaved, their garments torn, and beating their breasts, with manna and frankincense in their hands to bring into the house of the Lord.
verses.48:6: And Ishmael went out to meet them—they were walking along and weeping—and he said to them, "Come in to Gedaliah."
verses.48:7: And it came to pass, when they came into the midst of the city, that he slaughtered them into the cistern.
verses.48:8: But ten men were found there, and they said to Ishmael, "Do not slay us, for we have treasures in the field—wheat and barley, honey and oil." So he passed by and did not slay them among their brethren.
verses.48:9: Now the cistern into which Ishmael cast all those whom he had struck down—this is a great cistern which King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel; this Ishmael filled with the slain.
verses.48:10: Then Ishmael turned back all the people who remained in Mizpah, and the daughters of the king, whom the captain of the guard had entrusted to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, and he departed to the region beyond the sons of Ammon.
verses.48:11: Now Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael had done.
verses.48:12: And they led out all their army and went to fight against him, and they found him by the great waters in Gibeon.
verses.48:13: And it came to pass, when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan and the commanders of the force that was with him,
verses.48:14: that they turned back to Johanan.
verses.48:15: And Ishmael escaped with eight men, and departed to the sons of Ammon.
verses.48:16: Then Johanan and all the commanders of the forces who were with him took all the remnant of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael, mighty men of war, and the women, and the rest, and the eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon,
verses.48:17: and they departed and stayed in Gaberochamaa, which is near Bethlehem, in order to go into Egypt
verses.48:18: from before the Chaldeans, for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael had struck down Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon had appointed in the land.
verses.49:1: Now all the commanders of the forces, and Johanan, and Azariah the son of Maaseiah, and all the people from the least even to the greatest, came near
verses.49:2: to Jeremiah the prophet and said to him, "Let our plea for mercy now fall before you, and pray to the Lord your God concerning this remnant; for we are left but a few out of many, as your eyes see,
verses.49:3: and may the Lord your God declare to us the way in which we should walk, and the word which we should do."
verses.49:4: Then Jeremiah said to them, "I have heard. Behold, I will pray to the Lord our God according to your words; and it shall come to pass that whatever word the Lord answers, I will declare to you. I will not conceal a word from you."
verses.49:5: And they said to Jeremiah, "Let the Lord be a righteous and faithful witness among us, if we do not act according to every word that the Lord sends to us.
verses.49:6: Whether it is good or whether it is evil, we will heed the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we send you, that it may be better for us, because we will heed the voice of the Lord our God."
verses.49:7: And it came to pass after ten days that the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
verses.49:8: Then he called Johanan and the commanders of the forces, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
verses.49:9: and said to them, "Thus says the Lord:
verses.49:10: 'If you indeed remain in this land, I will build you up and will not tear you down, and I will plant you and will not pluck you up; for I have relented concerning the evils that I have done to you.
verses.49:11: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid,' says the Lord, 'for I am with you to rescue you and to save you from their hand.
verses.49:12: And I will grant you mercy, and I will have mercy on you, and I will bring you back to your own land.'
verses.49:13: But if you say, 'We will not remain in this land,' so as not to obey the voice of the Lord,
verses.49:14: 'because we will enter the land of Egypt, and we shall not see war, nor hear the sound of a trumpet, nor hunger for bread, and there we will dwell'—
verses.49:15: therefore hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: 'If you set your face toward Egypt and enter there to dwell,
verses.49:16: then it shall come to pass that the sword which you fear shall find you in the land of Egypt, and the famine about which you are anxious shall overtake you right behind you in Egypt, and there you shall die.
verses.49:17: And so it shall be with all the men and all the foreigners who set their face toward the land of Egypt to dwell there: they shall perish by the sword and by the famine, and not one of them shall escape from the evils that I am bringing upon them.'
verses.49:18: For thus says the Lord: 'Just as My wrath was poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so My wrath shall be poured out upon you when you enter Egypt; and you shall become an untrodden waste, and in subjection, and a curse, and a reproach, and you shall no longer see this place.'
verses.49:19: These are the things which the Lord has spoken concerning you, O remnant of Judah: 'Do not enter Egypt.' And now you shall surely know
verses.49:20: that you acted wickedly in your souls when you sent me, saying, 'Pray for us to the Lord,' and, 'According to all that the Lord speaks to you, we will do.'
verses.49:21: Yet you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord in that for which He sent me to you.
verses.49:22: Now therefore by the sword and by the famine you shall perish in the place where you desire to go and dwell."
verses.50:1: Now it came to pass, when Jeremiah had finished speaking to the people all the words of the Lord, for which the Lord had sent him to them—all these words—
verses.50:2: that Azariah the son of Maaseiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the men who addressed Jeremiah spoke, saying, "You speak falsely! The Lord has not sent you to us, saying, 'Do not enter Egypt to dwell there,'
verses.50:3: but rather Baruch the son of Neriah is inciting you against us, that you may deliver us into the hands of the Chaldeans, to put us to death and to carry us away captive to Babylon."
verses.50:4: So Johanan, and all the commanders of the forces, and all the people did not obey the voice of the Lord, to dwell in the land of Judah.
verses.50:5: And Johanan and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Judah who had returned to dwell in the land—
verses.50:6: the mighty men, and the women, and the rest, and the daughters of the king, and the souls whom Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah—
verses.50:7: and they entered Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of the Lord; and they came into Tahpanhes.
verses.50:8: Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.50:9: "Take for yourself large stones and hide them in the entranceway, at the gate of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah,
verses.50:10: and you shall say, 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am sending and will bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he shall set his throne upon these stones which you have hidden, and he shall lift up his weapons against them.
verses.50:11: And he shall enter and strike the land of Egypt: such as are for death, to death; and such as are for captivity, to captivity; and such as are for the sword, to the sword.
verses.50:12: And he shall kindle a fire in the houses of their gods, and he shall burn them and carry them away captive; and he shall delouse the land of Egypt just as a shepherd delouses his garment, and he shall go forth in peace.
verses.50:13: And he shall shatter the pillars of Heliopolis that are in On, and their houses he shall burn up with fire.'"
verses.51:1: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews who dwelt in the land of Egypt, and those who resided in Migdol, and in Tahpanhes, and in the land of Pathros, saying:
verses.51:2: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: "You have seen all the evils which I brought upon Jerusalem and upon the cities of Judah; and behold, they are desolate, without inhabitants,
verses.51:3: because of their wickedness which they committed to provoke Me, going to burn incense to other gods whom you did not know.
verses.51:4: And I sent to you My servants the prophets early in the morning, and I sent them, saying, 'Do not do this thing of defilement which I hated.'
verses.51:5: Yet they did not listen, nor did they incline their ear to turn away from their evils, so as not to burn incense to other gods.
verses.51:6: Therefore My wrath and My fury poured down, and kindled in the gates of Judah and outside Jerusalem; and they became a desolation and an untrodden waste, as it is this day."
verses.51:7: And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: "Why do you commit great evils against your own souls, to cut off from you man and woman, infant and nursing child, from the midst of Judah, so that not one of you is left remaining,
verses.51:8: provoking Me by the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have come to dwell, that you may be cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
verses.51:9: Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of your rulers, and the evils of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and outside Jerusalem?
verses.51:10: And they have not ceased to this day, nor have they held fast to My ordinances which I set before their fathers."
verses.51:11: Therefore thus says the Lord: "Behold, I set My face
verses.51:12: to destroy all the remnant who are in Egypt; and they shall fall by the sword and by famine, and they shall perish, from the least to the greatest, and they shall become a reproach, and a destruction, and a curse.
verses.51:13: And I will punish those who dwell in the land of Egypt, as I punished Jerusalem, by the sword and by famine;
verses.51:14: and not one of the remnant of Judah who sojourn in the land of Egypt shall be saved to return to the land of Judah, to which they hope in their souls to return; they shall by no means return, except those who escape."
verses.51:15: Then all the men who knew that their wives burned incense, and all the women, a great assembly, and all the people who dwelt in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
verses.51:16: "As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you!
verses.51:17: For we will surely perform every word that shall proceed from our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her, just as we did—we and our fathers, our kings and our rulers—in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem; for then we were filled with bread, and we fared well, and we saw no evil.
verses.51:18: But since we ceased burning incense to the queen of heaven, we have all been brought low, and we have perished by the sword and by famine.
verses.51:19: And since we burn incense to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands?"
verses.51:20: Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people—to the mighty men, and to the women, and to all the people who had answered him with words—saying,
verses.51:21: "Did not the Lord remember the incense which we burned in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your rulers, and the people of the land—and did it not come into His heart?
verses.51:22: So the Lord could no longer bear it, because of the wickedness of your deeds and because of the abominations which you committed; therefore your land became a desolation, and an untrodden waste, and a curse, as it is on this day,
verses.51:23: because of the incense you burned and the ways you sinned against the Lord; and you did not listen to the voice of the Lord, nor did you walk in His ordinances, and in the law, and in His testimonies; therefore these evils have overtaken you."
verses.51:24: Moreover Jeremiah said to the people and to the women, "Hear the word of the Lord."
verses.51:25: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: "You women have spoken with your mouth and fulfilled it with your hands, saying, 'We will surely perform our vows which we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.' You have surely stood firm in your vows, and you have surely performed them."
verses.51:26: Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt: "Behold, I have sworn by My great name," says the Lord, "that My name shall no longer be in the mouth of anyone of Judah to say, 'The Lord lives,' in all the land of Egypt.
verses.51:27: For I am watching over them to harm them and not to do them good; and all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt shall perish by the sword and by famine, until they are utterly consumed.
verses.51:28: Yet those who escape the sword shall return to the land of Judah, few in number; and the remnant of Judah who have settled in the land of Egypt to dwell there shall know whose word shall abide.
verses.51:29: And this shall be the sign to you, that I will punish you for evil."
verses.51:30: Thus says the Lord: "Behold, I give Hophra king of Egypt into the hands of his enemy and into the hands of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy and the one who sought his life."
verses.51:31: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in the book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah:
verses.51:32: Thus says the Lord concerning you, O Baruch:
verses.51:33: "You said, 'Woe to me, woe to me! For the Lord has added toil to my pain; I lay down in groanings, and I found no rest.'"
verses.51:34: Say to him, "Thus says the Lord: 'Behold, those whom I built, I tear down; and those whom I planted, I pluck up.
verses.51:35: And will you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them; for behold, I am bringing evils upon all flesh,' says the Lord, 'and I will give your life to you as a prize in every place wherever you go.'"
verses.52:1: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.52:4: Now it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the ninth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem; and they laid siege to it and built four-footed siege works all around it.
verses.52:5: And the city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah,
verses.52:6: on the ninth day of the month; and the famine grew severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.52:7: Then the city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by the way of the gate between the wall and the outer wall, which was by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were all around the city. And they went by the way toward the Arabah,
verses.52:8: but the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and they overtook him beyond Jericho; and all his servants were scattered from him.
verses.52:9: So they seized the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha; and he spoke to him with judgment.
verses.52:10: And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; and he also slew all the rulers of Judah in Deblatha.
verses.52:11: And he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in fetters; and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in the millhouse until the day he died.
verses.52:12: Now in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuzaradan the chief cook, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem,
verses.52:13: and he burned the house of the Lord and the king's house; and all the houses of the city, and every great house, he burned with fire.
verses.52:14: And the army of the Chaldeans that was with the chief cook tore down every wall of Jerusalem all around.
verses.52:16: And the chief cook left the remnant of the people behind as vinedressers and as farmers.
verses.52:17: And the Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, and took their bronze and carried it away to Babylon.
verses.52:18: Also the crown, and the bowls, and the fleshhooks, and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered,
verses.52:19: and the sapphoth, and the masmaroth, and the pouring vessels, and the lampstands, and the censers, and the ladles—whatever was of gold, in gold, and whatever was of silver, in silver—the chief cook took away.
verses.52:20: And the two pillars, and the one sea, and the twelve bronze calves beneath the sea, which King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord—the bronze of them was beyond weight.
verses.52:21: Now as for the pillars, the height of one pillar was thirty-five cubits, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled it, and its thickness was four fingers all around;
verses.52:22: and a bronze capital was upon them, and five cubits was the length, the height of one capital, with latticework and pomegranates upon the capital all around, all of bronze; and likewise for the second pillar, eight pomegranates to a cubit for the twelve cubits.
verses.52:23: And the pomegranates were ninety-six on one side, and all the pomegranates upon the latticework all around were one hundred.
verses.52:24: And the chief cook took the first priest, and the second priest, and the three who guarded the way;
verses.52:25: and one eunuch who was overseer of the men of war, and seven men of renown who were in the presence of the king, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the armies who acted as scribe for the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
verses.52:26: And Nebuzaradan the chief cook took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha.
verses.52:27: And the king of Babylon struck them down in Deblatha, in the land of Hamath.
verses.52:31: Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year after Jehoiakim king of Judah was carried into exile, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, that Ulaimadachar king of Babylon, in the year in which he began to reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiakim king of Judah and shaved him, and brought him out of the house where he was kept under guard;
verses.52:32: and he spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the kings who were with him in Babylon;
verses.52:33: and they changed his prison garment, and he ate bread continually before him all the days that he lived.
verses.52:34: And his allowance was given to him continually from the king of Babylon, from day to day, until the day he died.

notes.1:1: The Greek reads "The word of God which came upon Jeremiah" and singular "who dwelt" (referring to Jeremiah), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "The words of Jeremiah" and plural "who were in Anathoth."
notes.1:2: The Greek reads "Amos" here rather than "Amon" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:6: The Greek translates the Hebrew exclamation as "O You who are, Sovereign Lord" (Ho on despota Kyrie), echoing the divine self-revelation in Exodus 3:14.
notes.1:11: The Greek specifies a "nut tree" (karyine) rather than specifically an almond tree, and therefore does not mirror the Hebrew wordplay with "watching" in verse 12.
notes.2:2: The Greek omits verse 1, reads "the love of its perfection" (with masculine/neuter pronoun autou, "its/his"), and has "the Holy One of Israel" where the Hebrew reads "after Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown."
notes.2:7: The Greek renders the Hebrew term for "orchard/plentiful land" as the proper name "Carmel."
notes.2:16: The Greek reads "knew you and mocked you," diverging from the Hebrew "have broken the crown of your head."
notes.2:18: The Greek names the river "Gihon" (an ancient designation associated with the Nile) where the Hebrew reads "Shihor," and uses plural "rivers" rather than singular "the River."
notes.2:23: In verses 23-24, the Greek departs markedly from the Hebrew animal imagery, reading "in the burial ground" (polyandrion), "At evening her voice wailed," "carried away by the wind," and "in her humiliation."
notes.3:1: The Greek reads "that woman" and "with many shepherds," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "that land" and "with many lovers."
notes.3:2: The Greek compares Judah to "a forsaken crow," reflecting a vocalization of the Hebrew consonants as "raven/crow" rather than the Masoretic Text's "Arab in the wilderness."
notes.3:6: The Greek renders the designation as "the habitation of Israel" (also in 3:8 and 3:12), deriving it from the Hebrew root for dwelling rather than turning back ("backsliding Israel").
notes.3:19: The Greek opens with the prayerful exclamation "Let it be so, Lord!" before continuing with God's declaration of "an inheritance of God Almighty of the nations," differing notably from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:1: The Greek reads "from his mouth," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from My presence."
notes.4:11: The Greek reads "A spirit of wandering is in the wilderness" and "not toward what is pure, nor toward what is holy," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's scorching wind not meant to winnow or cleanse.
notes.4:23: The Greek summarizes the desolation of the earth concisely as "nothing," rendering the Hebrew phrase "without form and void."
notes.4:26: The Greek takes the Hebrew term as the proper place name "Carmel" rather than "the fruitful land," and describes the cities as "burned with fire" rather than broken down.
notes.5:6: Greek reads "a wolf even to the houses" and "shall be hunted down," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a wolf of the deserts" and "shall be torn in pieces."
notes.5:10: Greek commands the invaders to "leave behind her foundations, for they belong to the Lord," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("strip away her branches, for they are not the LORD's").
notes.5:16: Greek omits the opening clause "their quiver is like an open tomb" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and joins the first clause of verse 17 directly to "All of them are mighty."
notes.5:31: Greek reads "the priests have clapped with their hands" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the priests rule by their own authority."
notes.6:2: Greek reads "and your height shall be taken away, O daughter of Zion," diverging markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("I have likened the daughter of Zion to a lovely and delicate woman").
notes.6:11: Greek places this verse in the Lord's first-person voice ("I have filled My wrath... I will pour it out"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks in the prophet's voice ("I am full of the wrath of the LORD") followed by a command ("Pour it out").
notes.6:16: Greek specifies "the everlasting paths of the Lord" and promises "purification for your souls," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the ancient paths" and "rest for your souls."
notes.6:23: Greek adds "and chariots" and reads "like fire" for the advancing enemy, reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants rendered "like a man" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.7:2: The Greek text omits verse 1 and the narrative introduction of verse 2 found in the Hebrew, opening the chapter directly with the prophetic summons to Judea.
notes.7:4: The Greek repeats "the temple of the Lord" twice (rather than three times as in the Hebrew) and adds "for they will not profit you at all."
notes.7:10: The Greek reads "We have abstained from doing all these abominations," expressing a false claim of innocence rather than the Hebrew "We are delivered—to do all these abominations."
notes.7:12: The Greek text reads the aorist indicative "you went" (and "saw") rather than the Hebrew imperative "go now... and see."
notes.7:18: The Greek reads "the host of heaven" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the queen of heaven."
notes.8:6: The Greek imagery diverges from the Hebrew, depicting a runner who has stopped short in his course "like a sweat-drenched horse in his neighing."
notes.8:7: "Stork" renders Greek asida, a transliteration of the Hebrew name for the bird; the Greek also includes "the sparrows" alongside the turtledove and the swallow of the field.
notes.8:10: The Greek text omits the second half of verse 10 and all of verses 11-12, carrying the sentence directly into verse 13.
notes.8:18: In the Greek text, verse 18 completes the sentence begun by God in verse 17 rather than opening a separate lament by the prophet.
notes.8:23: This verse corresponds to Jeremiah 9:1 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and most modern English versions.
notes.9:5: Greek tokos epi tokō ("usury upon usury") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("your dwelling is in the midst of deceit").
notes.9:6: Greek hoti poiēsō ("for I will act") presents a declarative statement rather than the rhetorical question found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:10: Greek eis metoikian ("over to exile") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("a heap of ruins"), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.9:25: The Septuagint names "Idumea" alongside "Edom," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Judah" in place of "Idumea."
notes.10:9: The Septuagint omits verses 5–8 and 10 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text and combines the idol polemic here; "Mophaz" is the Greek proper name corresponding to Hebrew "Uphaz."
notes.10:13: Greek phōs ("light") stands where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "wind," and the opening clause connects directly to verse 12 without "when He utters His voice."
notes.10:17: Greek synēgagen ("He has gathered") and en eklektois ("in choice places") differ from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Gather up your wares from the ground, O inhabitant of the siege").
notes.10:20: Greek kai ta probata mou ("and my sheep") appears here where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "have gone forth from me."
notes.11:8: Verse 7 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text is absent in the Septuagint, which moves directly from verse 6 to the brief statement of verse 8.
notes.11:13: The Greek places the feminine article tē before "Baal" (as also in 11:17), reflecting the traditional substitution of the feminine Hebrew noun bosheth ("shame") for the name of Baal.
notes.11:16: Greek peritomēs ("pruning" or "circumcision") renders the olive-tree imagery differently from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("with the roar of a great tumult").
notes.11:19: Greek embalōmen xylon eis ton arton autou ("let us cast wood into his bread") reflects reading the Hebrew noun as "his bread" rather than "its fruit," a rendering often given Christological significance in early Christian interpretation.
notes.12:2: The Septuagint reads "they bore children" (eteknopoiesanto), reflecting a Hebrew Vorlage "they bore offspring" rather than the Masoretic Text's "they grow."
notes.12:5: The Septuagint reads "Your own feet run and weary you," understanding the Hebrew term as "feet" rather than "footmen" as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.12:9: Where the Masoretic Text speaks of a "speckled bird of prey," the Septuagint renders "a hyena's cave" (spelaion hyaines).
notes.13:14: The Septuagint reads "I will scatter them" and "I will not yearn after them," differing from the Masoretic Text's "I will dash them one against another" and "I will not pity."
notes.13:17: In the Septuagint the pronouns are second-person plural ("your soul," "your eyes") rather than first-person singular ("my soul," "my eye") as in the Masoretic Text, and the flock is "crushed" rather than "taken captive."
notes.13:18: The Septuagint renders the title as plural "those who rule" (tois dynasteuousin), whereas the Masoretic Text refers specifically to the queen mother.
notes.14:8: The Septuagint reads "like a native" (hos autochthon), contrasting with the Masoretic Text's "like a traveler."
notes.14:13: The Greek address Ho on, Kyrie ("O Existing One, Lord") echoes the Septuagint's rendering of the divine name in Exodus 3:14.
notes.14:17: The Septuagint uses a second-person plural command ("Bring down tears upon your eyes") rather than the first-person singular ("Let my eyes run down with tears") found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.15:7: The Septuagint reads "in dispersion" and third-person plural verbs ("they were made childless; they have destroyed My people because of their wickedness"), differing from the Masoretic Text ("with a winnowing fork... I have bereaved... I have destroyed").
notes.15:11: The Greek frames this verse as Jeremiah's protestation to the Master ("May it be so, O Master, while they prosper..."), whereas the Masoretic Text presents a divine assurance to the prophet.
notes.15:16: Continuing the sentence from verse 15, the Septuagint reads "from those who reject Your words; make an end of them," differing notably from the Masoretic Text ("Your words were found, and I ate them").
notes.15:19: The Greek pairs "precious" (timion) with "cheap" (axiou), using axios in its attested Koine sense of "inexpensive" or "of little worth" in contrast to what is costly.
notes.16:4: The Septuagint reads "for an example" (eis paradeigma, a public spectacle) rather than "as refuse" as in the Masoretic Text, and places the beasts and birds before the sword and famine.
notes.16:5: Greek thiasos denotes a ritual or banqueting company, here rendering the Hebrew funerary feasting association (marzeach).
notes.16:13: The Septuagint ends the verse with "other gods, who will not show you mercy," whereas the Masoretic Text has the Lord say "for I will not show you favor."
notes.17:5: The Septuagint omits verses 17:1-4 (present in the Masoretic Text) and begins chapter 17 directly with this verse.
notes.17:9: The Septuagint reads "Deep is the heart above all things, and he is a man," rendering the underlying Hebrew consonants as "deep" (batheia) and "man" (anthropos) rather than "deceitful" and "desperately sick."
notes.17:16: The Greek reads "I have not grown weary in following after You, nor have I desired the day of man," again understanding the Hebrew consonants as "man" rather than "woeful."
notes.17:26: Greek manna ("manna") here transliterates the Hebrew minchah ("grain offering"), appearing in the Septuagint alongside incense and frankincense.
notes.18:4: The Greek reads "fell" (epesen) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "was spoiled/marred," and in verse 3 renders the potter's wheel literally as "the stones" (ton lithon).
notes.18:7: Greek peras ("in the end" or "finally") renders Hebrew rega' ("at one instant" or "suddenly"); the same term recurs in verse 9.
notes.18:12: Greek andrioumetha ("we will act courageously" or "we will be resolute") stands where the Hebrew reads no'ash ("it is hopeless").
notes.18:14: Greek mastoi ("breasts," possibly referring to breast-shaped crags or peaks) reflects reading Hebrew saday ("field") as shaday ("breasts").
notes.18:18: Unlike the Hebrew ("let us not pay heed to any of his words"), the Greek omits the negative, depicting Jeremiah's opponents as listening intently to trap him.
notes.19:2: Greek polyandrion ("burial ground" or "common cemetery") renders the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, and "Gate of Tharseis" transliterates the gate name rendered "Potsherd Gate" in the Hebrew.
notes.19:6: Greek Diaptosis ("Downfall" or "Ruin") translates Hebrew Topheth, a wordplay echoed by the related participial forms in verses 12-14.
notes.19:7: Greek sphaxo ("I will slaughter") creates a direct verbal echo of "Burial Ground of the Slaughter" in verse 6, whereas the Hebrew reads "I will empty out" or "make void."
notes.20:2: Greek katarakten ("dungeon" or "trapdoor pit") stands where the Hebrew reads "stocks," and "the upper house set apart" appears instead of the Hebrew "Upper Gate of Benjamin."
notes.20:3: Greek Metoikos ("Exile" or "Migrant") renders the symbolic name given to Pashhur (Hebrew Magor-Missabib, "Terror on Every Side"), linking directly to the exile announced in verse 4.
notes.20:8: Greek "with my bitter word I shall laugh" diverges from the Hebrew ("whenever I speak, I cry out"), continuing the motif of mockery from verse 7.
notes.20:11: Greek noesai / enoesan ("understand") appears twice where the Hebrew reads "stumble" and "prosper," framing the enemies' defeat as a failure of comprehension.
notes.21:1: The Greek reads "Manassaeus" (Manassaiou), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Maaseiah."
notes.21:6: Greek thanatos ("death") regularly renders Hebrew deber ("pestilence") in Septuagint Jeremiah, both here and in 21:7.
notes.21:7: The Greek omits the specific mention of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and places the final verbs in the first person ("I will not spare... nor will I have compassion") rather than the third person as in the Hebrew.
notes.21:13: The Greek treats Hebrew tsur ("rock") as the proper name "Sor" and reads the following verb as "terrify" rather than "come down."
notes.22:12: The Greek uses the first person ("where I have exiled him") rather than the third-person plural ("where they have taken him captive") of the Hebrew.
notes.22:15: The Greek reads "Ahaz your father" where the Hebrew refers to competing in "cedar" and then asks about "your father," and it continues with third-person plural future verbs ("They shall not eat and they shall not drink").
notes.22:16: Whereas the Hebrew praises Josiah's justice and asks if that is not knowing the Lord, the Greek has negative plural verbs ("They did not know; they did not judge") and a negative conclusion ("that you do not know Me").
notes.22:20: Greek "to the region beyond the sea" interprets Hebrew Abarim ("regions beyond") as a geographical phrase rather than a proper place name.
notes.22:30: Greek ekkerykton ("outcast" or "proscribed") renders Hebrew ariri ("childless"), and the Greek text does not include the Hebrew clause "a man who shall not prosper in his days."
notes.23:6: Greek reads Κύριος Ἰωσέδεκ ("which the Lord shall call Him: Josedek"), transliterating the Messianic title rather than translating it, and closes the verse with the heading "Concerning the prophets." Also in 23:5, Greek ἀνατολή ("rising" or "dayspring") corresponds to the Hebrew title often rendered "Branch."
notes.23:8: In this Septuagint numbering, verse 23:7 is omitted and verse 23:8 combines the conclusion of the oracle against the prophets (MT 23:40) with the new-exodus promise (MT 23:7–8).
notes.23:10: The Greek text reads ὁ δρυμὸς αὐτῶν ("their forest" or "thicket"), likely an ancient textual variant for δρόμος ("course").
notes.23:31: The Greek reads "slumber their own slumber" (νυστάζοντας νυσταγμὸν αὐτῶν), reading the Hebrew consonants as a root for slumber rather than the Masoretic "utter an oracle."
notes.23:33: Greek λῆμμα ("burden" or "oracle") creates a wordplay with λαμβάνω ("take up") and ῥάσσω ("cast down") in verses 33 and 39.
notes.24:1: The Greek text reads τοὺς πλησίους ("the neighbors"), a variant alongside τοὺς πλουσίους ("the rich") in some Septuagint manuscripts, and renders the group known in the Hebrew text as "smiths" as δεσμώτας ("prisoners").
notes.24:9: The Greek reads διασκορπισμόν ("dispersion") and μῖσος ("hatred"), differing from the Masoretic readings "horror" and "taunt."
notes.25:3: The Greek text names Josiah's father as Ἀμὼς (Amos), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Amon.
notes.25:9: Throughout verses 1–12, the Septuagint lacks explicit references to Nebuchadnezzar and Babylon, referring instead to "a family from the north" and "that nation."
notes.25:10: The Greek reads ὀσμὴν μύρου ("the fragrance of ointment"), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew behind the Masoretic "sound of the millstones."
notes.25:14: In the Septuagint arrangement of Jeremiah, the oracles against the nations begin here with Elam, corresponding to Jeremiah 49:34–39 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.26:2: In the Septuagint, chapter 26 corresponds to Masoretic chapter 46 and begins at verse 2; "Charmeis" is the Greek form of Carchemish.
notes.26:14: The Septuagint reads "your bindweed" (Greek smilax, a climbing plant or yew) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "your surroundings."
notes.26:15: The Septuagint uniquely names "Apis," the sacred bull-deity of Memphis, as Egypt's "chosen calf," where the Hebrew text refers more generally to Egypt's mighty ones.
notes.26:16: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew phrase for "oppressing sword" as "the Greek sword" (as also in 27:16), reading the Hebrew consonants as referring to Greece (Ionia).
notes.26:17: "Saon Esbei Emoed" is the Septuagint's transliteration of the symbolic Hebrew name given to Pharaoh Necho, rather than a translation of its meaning.
notes.27:2: Septuagint chapter 27 corresponds to Masoretic chapter 50; the Greek adds the epithets "the fearless one" and "the delicate one" (cf. 26:28) and gives the Babylonian deity Merodach as "Maiodak."
notes.27:8: The Septuagint reads "dragons" (Greek drakontes) where the Hebrew text reads "he-goats" leading the flock.
notes.27:21: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew place names Merathaim and Pekod by their roots as "Bitterly" and "take vengeance."
notes.27:39: The Septuagint renders the desert creatures of the Hebrew text as "phantoms in the islands" and "daughters of sirens."
notes.27:44: "Gaithan" is the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew phrase for "enduring pasture" as a proper place name.
notes.28:2: Greek reads ὑβριστάς ("insolent men") and καθυβρίσουσιν ("shall deal insolently with her"), preserving the Septuagint cognate wordplay where the Masoretic Text reads "winnowers" who winnow her.
notes.28:5: Greek reads the plural τῶν ἁγίων Ἰσραήλ (which may mean "the holy ones of Israel" or "the holy things of Israel"), in contrast to the Masoretic Text's singular "the Holy One of Israel."
notes.28:16: Greek reads φῶς ("light") rather than "wind" (as in the Masoretic Text), and renders the opening clause εἰς φωνὴν ἔθετο ἦχος ὕδατος ("at a voice He placed a roar of water").
notes.28:20: Greek renders the opening clause verbally as διασκορπίζεις σύ μοι σκεύη πολέμου ("You scatter for Me weapons of war"), rather than the Masoretic Text's "You are My war-club and weapons of war."
notes.28:27: Where the Masoretic Text lists the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz, the Septuagint reads βασιλεῖς ἄρατε παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ, καὶ τοῖς Ἀσχαναζέοις ("raise up kings from Me, and to the Ashkenazites"), and renders the following term as βελοστάσεις ("siege engines").
notes.28:34: Greek reads κατέλαβέν με σκότος λεπτόν ("a thin darkness has overtaken me"), a distinctive Septuagint reading (widely regarded as an early Greek textual shift from σκεῦος κενόν, "empty vessel") where the Masoretic Text has "he has set me down as an empty vessel."
notes.28:44: Verses 45–48 of the Masoretic Text (Jeremiah 51:45–48) are absent in the Septuagint, so 28:49 follows directly after 28:44 and continues the sentence.
notes.28:58: Greek includes the negation οὐ κοπιάσουσιν ("shall not labor") and reads ἐν ἀρχῇ ("in the beginning"), whereas the Masoretic Text lacks the negation and reads "for fire."
notes.28:59: Greek calls Seraiah ἄρχων δώρων ("chief of the gifts"), reflecting a reading of Hebrew minchah ("gift/tribute") rather than menuchah ("quartermaster"), and states that he went "from Zedekiah" rather than "with Zedekiah."
notes.28:64: Greek reads ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν Χαλδαίων ("from the face of the Chaldeans") rather than "because of the calamity/evil" (as in the Masoretic Text and some Greek manuscripts), and concludes the chapter without the closing editorial line of Masoretic Jeremiah 51:64.
notes.29:1: Greek allophyloi literally means "foreigners" and is the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines.
notes.29:4: The Septuagint reads first-person "I will wipe out" and "the remnant of the islands," whereas the Masoretic Text has "to cut off from Tyre and Sidon" and "the coastland of Caphtor."
notes.29:5: The Septuagint reads "the Anakim" (Enakeim) where the Masoretic Text has "their valley," and in 29:6 uses epartheti ("be lifted up" or "be removed") where the Hebrew has "be still."
notes.30:1: Greek Idoumaia ("Idumea") corresponds to Hebrew Edom; throughout 30:1-16 the Septuagint preserves distinctive readings such as "their place has been deceived" (30:2), "by the hand of his brother, My neighbor" (30:4), "yet I shall live" (30:5), "in the midst of her" instead of Bozrah (30:7), "Etham" as a place name (30:13), and "the cry of the sea was not heard" (30:15).
notes.30:17: The Septuagint names the Ammonite deity "Melchol" (Hebrew Milcom/Malcam) and reads "Gilead" where the Masoretic Text has "Gad"; in 30:18 it has "her altars" instead of "her daughters/villages," and in 30:20 "the plains of the Anakim."
notes.30:23: The Septuagint renders Hebrew "kingdoms of Hazor" as "queen of the court" (continuing "the court" in 30:25, 28) and has plesate ("fill") where the Hebrew has "plunder" (some view plesate as an early Greek scribal variant for plexate, "strike"). "Kedem" transliterates the Hebrew name meaning "the East."
notes.30:27: The Greek manuscript reads kekramenous (literally "mingled"), an early scribal metathesis for kekarmenous ("shorn/clipped"), referring to desert tribes who clipped the hair on their temples.
notes.30:29: The Septuagint reads "Themar" where the Masoretic Text has "Hamath," and in 30:31-33 reads "They have loved a village" and "the quarters of the son of Hader" (corresponding to Hebrew "the palaces of Ben-Hadad").
notes.31:1: Greek reads two proper names, Hamath and Agath, where the Masoretic Text has "the stronghold is put to shame and dismayed."
notes.31:4: Greek reads the place name Zogora (Zoar) rather than "her little ones," and in verse 5 transliterates Aloth for the ascent of Luhith; similar Septuagint-distinct place names appear in verses 21, 31, 32, and 34.
notes.31:26: Greek reads "strike with his hand" rather than the Masoretic "wallow in his vomit."
notes.31:33: Greek renders the underlying Hebrew vintage shout (hedad) with the feminine demonstrative "these" (haide); compare "these" (hoide) in 32:30.
notes.31:41: Greek reads the city Ekron (Akkaron) here rather than Kerioth, and verse 40 omits the Masoretic eagle imagery.
notes.32:15: In the Septuagint order, chapter 32 begins at verse 15 (parallel to Masoretic Jeremiah 25:15-38); Greek reads "unmixed wine" rather than "wine of wrath."
notes.32:23: Greek reads the distinct proper name Rhos where the Masoretic Text has Buz.
notes.32:26: Greek reads "from the east" rather than "of the north," and in verse 25 reads "the Persians" rather than "the Medes."
notes.32:30: Greek reads the demonstrative "these" (hoide) where the underlying Hebrew has hedad, the shout of grape-treaders; compare 31:33.
notes.32:34: Greek reads "like the chosen rams" rather than the Masoretic "like a precious vessel."
notes.33:2: Greek reads "all the Judeans" (hapasi tois Ioudaiois), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "all the cities of Judah."
notes.33:7: Here and throughout chapters 33–35 (33:8, 11, 16; 34:9; 35:1), the Septuagint explicitly calls Jeremiah's opponents "false prophets" (pseudoprophetai), where the Hebrew reads simply "prophets."
notes.33:18: Greek eis abaton ("an untrodden waste") renders Jerusalem's desolation in Micah's oracle (cf. Micah 3:12), differing from the Hebrew's "heaps of ruins."
